# midpoint_task (Resource)

A midPoint task (TaskType). The provider sets the execution state only when it creates the task; suspending or resuming it in midPoint is an operation, not a change of configuration, and is never drift. Assignments (in extra) are compared only when the task configures some: midPoint assigns a task the archetype of its activity when it runs, so an assignment added in midPoint to a task that configures none is not drift.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A recompute task for contractors. It is created suspended (the default)
# and started from midPoint; suspending or resuming it there is not drift.
resource "midpoint_task" "recompute_contractors" {
  name        = "Recompute contractors"
  description = "Recomputes every contractor."

  activity = {
    work = {
      recomputation = {
        objects = {
          type  = "UserType"
          query = { filter = { text = "subtype = \"contractor\"" } }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# A recurring recompute of all users at 02:00, owned by the administrator.
# It is created suspended: resume it in midPoint to start the schedule
# (initial_execution_state = "runnable" would start it on create).
resource "midpoint_task" "nightly" {
  name                    = "Nightly recompute"
  owner                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002" # administrator
  initial_execution_state = "suspended"
  binding                 = "loose"

  schedule = {
    recurrence      = "recurring"
    cronLikePattern = "0 0 2 * * ?"
  }

  activity = {
    work = {
      recomputation = {
        objects = { type = "UserType" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Object name.

### Optional

- `activity` (Dynamic) Activity definition (activity) in midPoint naming, e.g. yamldecode(file("recompute.yaml")).
- `adopt_existing` (Boolean) When an object with the configured oid already exists, adopt it into state and apply the configuration to it as an update instead of failing. The configuration must describe the whole object: items midPoint holds that are not configured (other than server-managed ones) are removed on the first apply. The plan warns that the object will be adopted and lists the changes the update will send. Meant for the midPoint built-ins a catalogue customizes. Without it, creating an object whose oid already exists fails and nothing is written. While it is true, destroying the object fails unless force_destroy is set: an adopted object is not Terraform's to delete. Remove it from state with a removed block (lifecycle { destroy = false }) to stop managing it. Importing a midPoint built-in (oid 00000000-0000-0000-0000-*) records it as adopted (true); any other import records false. Defaults to false.
- `binding` (String) Binding (binding): loose or tight. When unset midPoint defaults it (loose) and it is not compared. An imported task reads it back as null until it is configured, so a config that sets it plans one no-op update after the import.
- `description` (String) Description.
- `extra` (Dynamic) Other midPoint items, merged at the object root, in midPoint naming (camelCase, as in the REST API), e.g. yamldecode(file("extra.yaml")). An item must not also be set by a typed attribute.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Delete the object even when it was adopted with adopt_existing = true, which is refused otherwise. There is no reference check for this type. Defaults to false.
- `initial_execution_state` (String) Execution state the task is created in: suspended (the default) or runnable. It is written only on create; later suspending or resuming the task in midPoint is not drift. Changing it re-creates a task the provider created, and removing the line counts as a change (back to suspended). An imported or adopted task is never replaced for it: an import records suspended, an adoption the configured value, and a change only updates the state.
- `oid` (String) Object OID. When unset midPoint generates one. Changing it replaces the object. Creating an object whose oid already exists fails unless adopt_existing is set.
- `options` (List of String) midPoint execution options sent on create and update, e.g. raw, isImport, reevaluateSearchFilters. When unset, the provider default_options entry for task applies, else the built-in defaults: isImport on create and none on update. An empty list sends no options. overwrite is sent only when listed here; reevaluateSearchFilters is added to any write that sends a reference with a filter and no oid.
- `owner` (String) OID of the owning user (ownerRef). When unset midPoint makes the calling user the owner, and the owner is not compared. An imported task reads it back as null until it is configured, so a config that sets it plans one no-op update after the import.
- `recurrence` (String) Recurrence (recurrence): single or recurring.
- `schedule` (Dynamic) Schedule (schedule) in midPoint naming, e.g. { recurrence = "recurring", interval = 3600 }.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The object OID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the object OID. An imported task records
# initial_execution_state as suspended and is never re-created for it.
# owner and binding read back as null until they are configured, so a
# config that sets them plans one no-op update after the import.
terraform import midpoint_task.recompute_contractors 6a4c2b1e-3f0d-4b8a-9c7e-1d2f3a4b5c6d
```
